precepts.point: This is why you must vacate and run from Christianity as fast as possible, not ease out over years of so-called research. Once you know the man-made religions teach no commandments while our people die by the thousands, you should run to this truth and start keeping the commandments, because this is your life.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” It has been the same since the days of old: “All the commandments which I command thee this day shall ye observe to do, that ye may live”. The commandments are life; everything else brings death to us, and the commandments ultimately lead to eternal life.

This is why you must vacate and run from Christianity as fast as possible, not ease out over years of so-called research. Once you know the man-made religions teach no commandments while our people die by the thousands, you should run to this truth and start keeping the commandments, because this is your life.

precepts.point: Far too many tuck and run when the Most High is proving them; he never gives us something we are not able to overcome, and through Israel's schools, classes, and daily teaching he is giving you the way to bear the temptation. Prove to him that you will endure it, love him, and persevere; hard times are the perfect segue back into the vomit you came out of if you do not stand.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.”

The forty years in the wilderness were “to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no.” Trials and tribulations in this flesh are the Most High proving us the same way, whether a lost spouse, family separating from you, a lost job, or strife with friends.

Far too many tuck and run when the Most High is proving them. He never gives us something we are not able to overcome, and through Israel's schools, classes and daily teaching he is giving you the way to bear the temptation. Prove to him that you will endure it, love him and persevere; hard times are the perfect segue back into the vomit you came out of if you do not stand.

precepts.text: Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth; if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
precepts.point: This is why Esau has no judgment on him like Israel has: they are not the sons, so the Most High is not chastening them. You cannot do what the other nations do; when we get that in our heads we will be in a far better situation as a people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?”

Moses says the same: “as a man chasteneth his son, so the Lord thy God chasteneth thee.” You do wrong, you get punished, exactly as a father raises his children. Who is more experienced than the Most High, the Ancient of days? There is no way we can tell him through our actions that we know what is right for us.

“But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.” This is why Esau has no judgment on him like Israel has: they are not the sons, so the Most High is not chastening them. You cannot do what the other nations do; when we get that in our heads we will be in a far better situation as a people.

precepts.text: No chastening for the present seemeth joyous, but grievous; nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
precepts.point: This is why Esau has no judgment on him like Israel has: they are not the sons, so the Most High is not chastening them. You cannot do what the other nations do; when we get that in our heads we will be in a far better situation as a people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.”

Moses says the same: “as a man chasteneth his son, so the Lord thy God chasteneth thee.” It is not joyous when you do wrong and get punished, but that is exactly how a father raises his children, and afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness. Who is more experienced than the Most High, the Ancient of days? There is no way we can tell him through our actions that we know what is right for us. The other nations are not chastened because they are not the sons; Israel is, and we cannot do what they do.

precepts.text: The desolate land shall be tilled and become like the garden of Eden, and when Israel learns the law they shall lothe themselves in their own sight for their iniquities; I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.
precepts.point: The Most High says he will return the land to its original form, like the garden of Eden; that is a precept in itself, for the garden of Eden is Jerusalem, the land of Israel, the land of milk and honey.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
Verses 7 through 9 are the precept for describing the land of milk and honey: “a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and depths that spring out of valleys and hills; A land of wheat, and barley, and vines, and fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of oil olive, and honey”, where “thou shalt eat bread without scarceness”, whose stones are iron and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass. Write it down and use it.

Right now the land is not flowing with milk and honey: the place is desolate, full of desert places, and much of its food is imported, exactly as the prophecy requires until the Most High restores it. Ezekiel gives the restoring: “I will call for the corn, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that ye shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen.”

“And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. The Most High says he will return the land to its original form, like the garden of Eden; that is a precept in itself, for the garden of Eden is Jerusalem, the land of Israel, the land of milk and honey.

And when Israel learns the law: “Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.” “Not for your sakes do I this, saith the Lord God”. It is sure: “I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.”

precepts.text: The fiery serpents of the wilderness: the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and much people of Israel died.
precepts.point: He led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents and scorpions and drought, brought thee water out of the rock of flint, and fed thee with manna, to humble thee and to prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.” These are the fiery serpents of the wilderness.

Moses reminds Israel who led them “through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water”. The serpents were real, sent by the Lord, and much people of Israel died of them. Yet he brought forth water out of the rock of flint and fed them with manna, to humble them and to prove them, “to do thee good at thy latter end”.

precepts.text: The devil shewed Christ all the kingdoms of the world and said, All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever I will I give it: if thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.
precepts.point: Who blesses everybody that does not keep the commandments and still gets everything they desire? Satan says come as you are; whoever wants power, fame, and money in this world without obeying God can have it from him, and you will pay the piper when you meet Christ. Share these precepts with your family.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

Who blesses everybody that does not keep the commandments and still gets everything they desire? Satan says come as you are. Whoever wants power, fame and money in this world without obeying God can have it from him, and you will pay the piper when you meet Christ.

Here is Christianity wrapped up in a few scriptures: “thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth.” They keep no commandments and then boast, look what we have done, look at this job, look at all this stuff, as if the Most High gave them that power. But “it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant”. The power to get wealth belongs to the covenant; if you forget God and keep no commandments, it was not God blessing you. Share these precepts with your family.

precepts.point: Who blesses everybody that does not keep the commandments and still gets everything they desire? Satan says come as you are; whoever wants power, fame, and money in this world without obeying God can have it from him, and you will pay the piper when you meet Christ. note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“For as the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, saith the Lord; that they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear.”

Our very life cleaves to the Most High, as the girdle cleaves to the loins of a man; yet the people followed the religions instead, and would not hear. That is forgetting the Lord thy God, “for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant”: the power belongs to the covenant, to the people that cleave unto him. Keep no commandments and boast of what thine own hand has gotten, and it was not God blessing you.

precepts.text: Lest when thou hast eaten and art full and all thou hast is multiplied, thine heart be lifted up and thou forget the Lord thy God.
precepts.point: With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God; we get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”. Jeshurun is Israel. Waxing fat is not about being overweight; Deuteronomy 8 explains it: “Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein; And when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied; Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage”.

That is what it means to wax fat, grow thick and be covered with fatness: full, housed, herds and silver and gold multiplied, and the heart lifted up. With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God. We get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High. That is how Israel “forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation”: forgetting the one who brought us out of the house of bondage.

precepts.text: Beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God in not keeping his commandments; the warning was given before they ever entered the land.
precepts.point: The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
The Lord says the people are too many “lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me.” That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think, and he warned about it before they ever entered the land: “Beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God, in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command thee this day.”

Forgetting the Lord begins with not keeping his commandments, and it ends with a man saying his own hand saved him. Thinning the army was the Lord keeping Israel from that very thing.

precepts.text: Lest thine heart be lifted up and thou say in thine heart, my power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth; thou shalt remember the Lord thy God, for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.
precepts.point: The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
Here is the heart the Lord was guarding against when he sent twenty and two thousand home: “Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; Who led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint; Who fed thee in the wilderness with manna, which thy fathers knew not, that he might humble thee, and that he might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end.”

The danger: “And thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth.” That is the same as “Mine own hand hath saved me.” The correction: “But thou shalt remember the Lord thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day.”

That is why God always lowered the numbers going into battle, so Israel would know it was by the Lord's strength that we overcame our enemies. And it is going to be the same thing again: few numbers going into battle against the nations when that time comes.

precepts.text: The law Christ quoted, written to Israel in the wilderness.
precepts.point: The formula is given here. The flesh is weak and profits nothing; the spirit is strengthened by the word, and that is how the temptation is endured.

note.label: Matthew 4: The Temptation in the Wilderness and the Calling of the Fishers

precepts.why:
Christ answered the tempter with what is written, and this is where it is written, in the law given to Israel in the wilderness: “man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord doth man live.”

Moses tells Israel why the Most High “suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna”: “that he might make thee know” this very thing. Israel was made hungry in the wilderness to learn it, and Christ, hungry in the wilderness, lived by it. He did not answer the devil with his own words but with the law, “It is written”.

precepts.text: The verse he went back to, written to Israel in the wilderness.
precepts.point: He answers with the law: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

note.label: Luke 4: The Temptation and the Reading at Nazareth

precepts.why:
Full of the Holy Ghost, Christ was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, forty days tempted of the devil, and ate nothing. When the devil said “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread”, he answered with the law: “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.”

This is the verse he went back to, written to Israel in the wilderness: “And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord doth man live.” Israel was humbled and suffered to hunger in the wilderness so they would learn that lesson; Christ, hungering in the wilderness, stood on it. Man lives by every word out of the mouth of the Lord, and Christ answered the devil with that word.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

points: “As the nations which the Lord destroyeth before your face, so shall ye perish”. The same way we watched the Most High destroy those nations, he would destroy us when we turned our backs on his laws. Did it happen? You damn right that happened. He destroyed the nations for sin, and we did the same things they did. We're still doing them and wondering why we're in this condition.

“because ye would not be obedient unto the voice of the Lord your God.” We black people are the most rebellious people on the planet when it comes to God's laws. We don't want to hear it. A sister asks whether the Most High will really kill her just because she's wearing pants, showing her behind or cleavage. In her mind nothing's wrong with it. Those who control the narrative control the mind. Society tells you nothing will happen. You can be a hoe the whole week, dress modestly on Sunday, and a pastor makes you feel good. Sleep with hundreds of men; social media says nothing's wrong. A sister says she wants your baby but doesn't want to marry you.

I came here at fourteen. Back in Haiti, a girl in my neighborhood got pregnant before marriage. Her father made the young man marry her, found money for a visa, and shipped her to the United States anyway because she'd brought shame on the family. I knew young men who died because the girls' fathers killed them. Get a daughter pregnant, refuse to marry her when the father comes to your family, and they kill you. That's the society I grew up in. In our household with five brothers, my mother said she wasn't losing any sons: you sleep with her, you will marry her. If you don't want her, don't sleep with her. I'm not losing you over foolishness.

Look at society today: where the hell did these people come from? Twenty years ago I wouldn't have believed America would look like this. It portrays itself as a Christian, righteous nation. There's nothing righteous about America. It's the most evil country on the planet. This is where Satan's city is.
